desks.Dividends: Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7%), payable Dec 10 — its 24th consecutive annual increase, yield 0.77%. Nvidia declared its Dec 2 ex-date yesterday ($0.25, unchanged), payable Dec 23. SPY and QQQ December distributions are undeclared. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia beat and raised, then sold off: revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y) vs about $109.1B consensus, non-GAAP EPS $2.68 vs $2.47, Q4 guidance $130.0B (+/-3%) vs about $125.1B consensus — but the stock faded a +2.4% open to close -2.89% at $150.96, about 1.5% above its 52-week low. The market is discounting the Q4 gross-margin step-down (71-72% guided vs 74.8% printed), zero China Data Center revenue in the guide, and leadership uncertainty under interim CEO Colette Kress. Cash flag: operating cash flow $48.3B vs net income $65.3B; DSO rose 60 to 64 days. No watchlist name reports earnings in the next two weeks.
desks.Futures: The EIA weekly report showed a broad-based build far above consensus: crude +3.4M barrels vs +0.058M expected, gasoline +5.2M vs +1.6M. WTI fell 4.45% to $82.18 and Brent 4.42% to $89.02, even as US-Iran fire was exchanged Tue and Strait of Hormuz traffic sat near zero (5 crossings Sat, 0 Sun vs 31 the prior weekend). Physical surplus is dominating war premium for now; the IEA expects the global market back in surplus in Q4. Next EIA weekly is Wed Nov 25; the natural gas storage report lands Thu Nov 19 at 10:30 ET.
desks.Parity: No parity violation was found. A live SPY at-the-money put-call parity check held within 2-3 cents on 0-DTE options — bid/ask noise, not a violation. No new index-methodology document and no new published parity-violation analysis since yesterday. The standing watch item is the S&P Dow Jones growth/value methodology revamp, announced Oct 23, effective at the annual reconstitution before the open Dec 21, with preliminary files Dec 4; it changes index composition, not parity math.
desks.Premium: Nvidia implied vol crushed 138.2% to 61.8% across the earnings print, and no binary event is left in the window for any watchlist name. Front-end implied vol stays elevated on QQQ, MSFT, Nvidia and Tesla — a post-crash regime surface, not event premium. Every IV-versus-realized verdict remains WINDOW-CONTINGENT: the Nov 5 crash day still drives 34.6-49.6% of each 20-day realized-variance window. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
desks.Quant lab: Seven new candidates were ledgered (#298-304) from the Nov 16-17 arXiv window, run max 60 — nothing TEST- or INTEGRATE-ready. The top item is #298 (Chen et al, conditional-gamma pricing of leveraged ETF options, score 60, WATCH): it builds the LETF vol surface from the index smile and reports pricing inside market bid-ask at most TQQQ strikes, source-reported and UNVERIFIED. #299 revisits Roll's R-squared 40 years later (score 59, WATCH). Four WATCH, three ARCHIVE. Re-checks showed no version movement on #294, #292, #207 or #206.

items.detail: The Nov 18 minutes resolve the Nov 13 open check hawkish, not dovish: 'almost all participants judged that... further action to raise the target range... would likely be appropriate,' and 'a couple' said a hike of more than 25bp 'could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable.' The 10-2 hold understated the tightening lean. Governor Waller went public for 50bp this morning. Desk 7 call holds and strengthens: a 25bp hike Dec 9, tally now 5 HIKE / 0 CUT / 5 NEUTRAL — housing starts flipped CUT to NEUTRAL on the Oct print (1,309k, +9.9% m/m). Kalshi prices the 25bp hike at $0.91 and the more-than-25bp tail at $0.08, doubled intraday from $0.04.
items.title: FOMC minutes resolve hawkish — Desk 7 strengthens to 5 HIKE / 0 CUT / 5 NEUTRAL

WTI fell 4.45% to $82.18 and Brent 4.42% to $89.02 on the day, even with US-Iran fire exchanged Tue and Hormuz traffic near zero. The market is pricing the EIA surplus signal over the war-risk signal. The Cushing draw (-1.2M) against a national build argues the glut is coastal and refined-product-side, not a hub bottleneck.
